title: Crime ring busted in SoCal after stealing more than $22 million in cargo, mostly Nike shoes and Milwaukee tools, from trains: DOJ
text:
Crime ring busted in SoCal after stealing more than $22 million in cargo, mostly Nike shoes and Milwaukee tools, from trains: DOJ - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Major crime ring busted in SoCal after stealing more than $22 million in cargo from trains, DOJ says 
 A crime ring has been disrupted in Southern California after its members stole more than $22 million worth of merchandise from cargo trains, prosecutors said. By Kevin Ozebek Friday, November 20, 2026 12:26AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google ANAHEIM, Calif. (KABC) -- Authorities have disrupted a massive crime ring in Southern California after its members stole more than $22 million worth of merchandise, mostly Nike shoes and power tools, from cargo trains, federal prosecutors said.
 Fourteen defendants were named in a 48-page indictment handed down by a grand jury and filed in court on Nov. 12. The indictment was unsealed on Thursday.
 "Beginning on an unknown date, but no later than February 6, 2024, and continuing through at least November 2026, in Los Angeles and Orange Counties" and elsewhere, the defendants allegedly conspired to commit interstate railroad cargo theft, according to prosecutors.
 Those named in the indictment are accused of stealing millions worth of Nikes and Milwaukee power tools, among other property, that were imported into the United States through Los Angeles and Long Beach, which are home to the busiest ports in the country
 Most of the 14 defendants had been arrested as of Thursday morning, the Justice Department said. Several of them were being processed at the federal building in downtown L.A.
 "The scale of the theft is staggering," First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement. "We have charged a crew of 14 in a scheme to steal more than $22.5 million in cargo from at least three dozen freight trains in Southern California. We will prosecute the people who raid these trains and those who knowingly turn stolen cargo into cash."
 Attached to the indictment was a video that appeared to show a masked burglar using a handheld electrical saw to cut through the lock of a cargo container -- emitting a shower of sparks -- while the train was in motion.
 The men would disable the trains at a planned location by busting the brakes, the indictment alleged, at which point the goods would be offloaded onto trucks. The goods were then peddled to an unnamed company that would resell the stolen merchandise for profit.

 Photos released by prosecutors allegedly show the defendants holding massive stacks of cash that was generated by the sale of the stolen goods.
 In group chats, the men shared numerous photos and videos of themselves busting into the hulking train cars, and posing with wads of cash and stolen merchandise. They also shared AI photos of themselves captioned "Los Trenes," which means the trains in Spanish, beneath glamorized photos of men throwing boxes of shoes off trains into nearby cars while police helicopters descended overhead.
 "This historic indictment, following a 14-month investigation assisted by our Bureau of Investigation, demonstrates the importance of dismantling entire criminal enterprises — from those stealing the cargo to those profiting from its resale," L.A. County Nathan J. Hochman said in a statement. "We are determined to protect this vital supply chain and ensure that goods reach their intended destinations, not the black market."
 The Associated Press contributed to this report.
